newsitem.title: USA: Strong demand boosts Penney debt deal to $2.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Strong demand boosts Penney debt deal to $2.5 bln.

text.p: Strong demand for J.C. Penney Co Inc's $2.5 billion multi-tranche debt offering triggered the deal to get upped in size three times to meet investor appetite for the paper, syndicate sources said.
"J.C. Penney's deal did very well across the curve with heavier demand for the shorter maturities seen," one syndicate source said.

The deal, which was initially slated to come as a $2.0 billion five-part debt deal, grew with the addition of a sixth tranche and increases to the three-year, five-year, 10-year and 40-year, putable in eight years, tranches, dealers said.
"Current tone in the market place is one that people looking for paper would rather see a shorter maturity over a longer tranche," said another syndicate source.
"The three-year issue was in very good shape...they could easily have sold a lot more of those," the source added.
Players said J.C. Penney's deal is expected to set the tone in the market for other issuers currently sidelined by higher borrowing costs.

"It's an important deal for the market," said another syndicate source. It's been kind of tough in corporates with spreads widening...these issues will be watched to see if they're able to hold spread in the secondary market."
"This will be a good yardstick for other issuers," the source added.

Last month, after the U.S. Federal Reserve Board's quarter-point rate hike, players cautiously moved to the sidelines as speculation that the Fed was embarking on a new tightening cycle swept through the market.
Meanwhile, the $2.5 billion debt offering, which was underwritten by lead manager Credit Suisse First Boston, included the following six tranches:
-$325 million three-year notes priced to yield a spread of 40 basis points,
-$700 million five-year notes priced to yield a spread of 50 basis points,
-$425 million 10-year notes priced to yield 70 basis points,
-$300 million 20-year debentures priced to yield a spread of 85 basis points,
-$350 million 30-year debentures, callable in 10 years, priced to yield 120 basis points,
-and the $400 million 40-year debentures, putable in eight years, priced to yield a spread of 50 basis points.
Some players said J.C. Penney's deal was currently aggressively bid for in the Street.

Proceeds from the offering will be used to refinance, on a long-term basis, $1.9 billion of short-term debt incurred by the company in connection with its acquisition of Eckerd Corp, according to J.C. Penney.
